# Adjudication Task — Chapter 699

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃699화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|구구구궁! 쿵!
  6|
  7|거센 진동을 이기지 못한 내궁의 석벽이 힘없이 허물어지고, 둔중한 소음을 떨어져 나간 철문이 지면을 후려친다.
  8|
  9|흡사 작은 동산이 무너지는 듯한 광경.
 10|
 11|그러나 미끄러지듯 잔해를 피한 백상의 신형은 쾌속하게 쏘아졌다.
 12|
 13|쉬이이익!
 14|
 15|전신을 스치는 바람. 곤두선 오감으로부터 비릿한 혈향(血香)과 곳곳에서 울려 퍼지는 비명이 전해진다.
 16|
 17|백상은 자신의 내부에서 요동치는 공력을 느끼며 심호흡했다.
 18|
 19|‘휩쓸려서는 안 된다.’
 20|
 21|마치 병풍처럼 내궁의 뒤에 우뚝 선 거대한 절벽.
 22|
 23|이제는 ‘균열’이라 불려야 할 절벽의 틈새에서 흘러나오고 있는 마기(魔氣)는 백상으로서도 쉽게 생각할 수 없었다.
 24|
 25|아니, 초절정 고수였기에 이렇게 내궁을 활보할 수 있다.
 26|
 27|마도(魔道)를 걷는 자가 아니라면, 어지간한 내가고수(內家高手)조차 저 마기의 영역에 들어선 순간 공력이 진탕되고 평정심을 잃었을 것이다.
 28|
 29|지금 이 순간, 비틀거리며 그를 막아선 한 중년인처럼.
 30|
 31|“구, 궁주? 궁주님이십니까?”
 32|
 33|모를 수 없는 얼굴이다.
 34|
 35|아비를 닮아 탐욕스럽고, 별다른 능력도 없이 부족장의 자리를 물려받아 호의호식하던 자.
 36|
 37|그렇기에 누구보다 열성적으로 백상을 지지했던 이였으니까.
 38|
 39|그러나 언제나 기름 낀 얼굴로 백상에게 아부로 가득한 미소를 건네던 그는, 지금 칠공(七空)에서 피를 흘리며 부르짖고 있었다.
 40|
 41|“제발, 제발 살려 주십시오! 전 아직 죽기 싫습……!”
 42|
 43|허우적거리며 뻗은 손이 새하얀 옷깃을 스친다. 중심을 잃고 쓰러진 부족장을 가만히 내려다보던 백상이 입을 열었다.
 44|
 45|“내가 왜 그래야 하지?”
 46|
 47|“구, 궁주?”
 48|
 49|“이미 알고 있었을 텐데. 내가 하려는 일이 남만에 크나큰 해가 된다는 것을.”
 50|
 51|“……!”
 52|
 53|“서로의 목적을 위해 합당한 대가를 주고받았으니, 부디 억울해하지는 말게.”
 54|
 55|나 역시 그러할 테니.
 56|
 57|입 밖으로 흘러나오지 않은 뒷말과 함께, 백상의 손가락 끝에서 지풍(指風)이 쏘아졌다.
 58|
 59|푸푹!
 60|
 61|천령개(天靈蓋)를 관통당한 부족장의 신형이 그대로 허물어진다.
 62|
 63|믿을 수 없다는 듯 눈을 부릅뜬 그의 눈빛은 죽어서도 백상에게 질문을 던지는 것 같았다.
 64|
 65|왜. 어째서.
 66|
 67|이 지옥도 앞에서도 당신은 그리 당당할 수 있느냐고.
 68|
 69|그리고 망자(亡者)의 물음에, 백상은 마음속으로 답했다.
 70|
 71|‘이미 각오했으니까.’
 72|
 73|그럼에도 입술 사이로 흘러나오는 숨결은 파르르 떨렸다.
 74|
 75|설령 저자가 제 목숨이 아니라 부족민들을 살려 달라 애걸했다면 살려 주었을까?
 76|
 77|아니, 어쩌면 편안한 죽음을 맞이했으니 형편없는 무공을 지닌 그에게는 오히려 자비였을지도 모른다.
 78|
 79|일만.
 80|
 81|무려 일만이다. 그 수많은 전사와 맹수가, 마기에 휩싸여 피를 흘리며 몸부림치고 있었다.
 82|
 83|그들이 내지르는 비명이 심장을 쥐어짜고, 칼날처럼 머릿속을 후비는 듯했다.
 84|
 85|하지만 백상은 걸음을 멈추지 않았다.
 86|
 87|쐐애애액!
 88|
 89|거침없이 쏘아진 신형이 비명이 깔린 드넓은 연무장을 가로질렀다.
 90|
 91|어릴 적 야율척과 함께 사고를 칠 때마다 숨어들었던 마구간도, 과실주를 훔치려 드나들었던 곳간도 한 줄기 바람이 되어 스쳐 지나갔다.
 92|
 93|복수심. 분노. 후회.
 94|
 95|보보(步步)마다 켜켜이 쌓여 온 감정들이 휘몰아친다.
 96|
 97|하나뿐인 아들을 전장으로 데려가지 않았더라면. 남천마후가 찾아온 그 날, 손을 맞잡는 대신 검을 뽑았더라면.
 98|
 99|누구보다, 심지어 백상 자신보다 그를 믿었던 하나뿐인 의형(義兄)에게만큼은 모든 진실을 털어놨더라면.
100|
101|혹은…….
102|
103|‘차라리 나 홀로 모든 것을 안고 자결했더라면.’
104|
105|저벅.
106|
107|어느 순간 쉼 없이 나아가던 발걸음이 멈췄다. 굳게 닫힌 문을 응시하는 눈은 어느새 붉게 충혈된 지 오래다.
108|
109|지금 백상의 뇌리에는 지난 밤 들었던 남천마후의 목소리가 울려 퍼지고 있었다.
110|
111|
112|
113|‘정오. 내일 정오야. 궁에 있는 모든 전사를 내궁으로 소집해.’
114|
115|‘내일…… 정오입니까.’
116|
117|‘그래. 당신이 맡은 역할은 거기까지야. 그 후의 일은 우리가 알아서…….’
118|
119|‘약조.’
120|
121|‘응?’
122|
123|‘약조를 지켜 주십시오. 오래전, 저와 했던 약조를.’
124|
125|‘너, 제법 건방지구나? 감히 어른이 말씀하시는데 말도 끊을 줄 알고.’
126|
127|
128|
129|남천마후는 웃었고, 백상은 한 치의 망설임도 없이 무릎을 꿇었다.
130|
131|그리고 그녀는 남만야수궁의 새로운 주인이 바닥에 머리를 찧는 것을 한참이나 지켜본 후에야 그가 간절히 원했던 대답을 들려주었다.
132|
133|
134|
135|‘예의 바른 아이에게는 상을 줘야겠지. 좋아, 대계가 시작되면 네 집무실로 돌아가.’
136|
137|‘……집무실이라면.’
138|
139|‘그래, 바로 이곳이지. 내가 한 약조는 그때 이루어질 거야.’
140|
141|
142|
143|웃음기 섞인 목소리가 귓가에서 흩어진다. 천천히, 아주 느리게 문을 향해 뻗어지는 백상의 하나뿐인 손이 파르르 떨렸다.
144|
145|‘어떻게?’라는 의문은 처음부터 들지 않았다.
146|
147|남천마후가, 암천이 그렇다면 그런 것이다.
148|
149|지금껏 그들이 보여 준 괴력난신(怪力亂神)과도 같은 일들을 생각하면 더더욱 그러했다.
150|
151|제아무리 많은 이목이 내궁에 깔려 있다 해도 약조는 지켜질 것이다.
152|
153|‘드디어.’
154|
155|드디어 이곳까지 왔다. 지그시 눈을 감자 아득한 기억의 파도가 밀려와 몸과 마음을 잠식한다.
156|
157|기나긴 인고(忍苦)의 세월.
158|
159|하지만 이 쓸쓸한 이야기에도 마지막 장은 존재했다. 잠에서 깬 듯 눈을 뜬 백상은 힘주어 문을 열었다.
160|
161|드륵.
162|
163|활짝 열어젖힌 문.
164|
165|그와 동시에 넓은 집무실이 백상의 시야에 들어왔다.
166|
167|옛 주인의 온기가 남아 있는 간소하면서도 투박한 집기와 오랜 세월을 간직한 탁자.
168|
169|더불어 이와 같은 집무실 풍경에 어울리지 않게 한 자리를 차지하고 있는 커다란 면경(面鏡).
170|
171|그리고. 그리고…….
172|
173|그것이 전부였다.
174|
175|‘없다. 아무것도.’
176|
177|믿을 수 없는 현실이 만근의 바위가 되어 한 사람을 짓눌렀다.
178|
179|텅 빈 공허한 눈빛으로 집무실을 바라보던 백상이 문득 실소를 흘렸다.
180|
181|“허. 허허. 허허허.”
182|
183|울지 못해 웃었고, 웃지 않을 수 없어 웃었다.
184|
185|남천마후는 약조를 지키지 않았다. 수십 년의 세월도. 그간 자신이 저지른 모든 일도 잿가루가 되어 흩날렸다.
186|
187|그 모든 것이, 결국 이렇게 끝난 것이다.
188|
189|“으하하하하!”
190|
191|백상은 파안대소(破顔大笑)했다. 마치 소년 시절로 돌아간 것처럼. 배를 움켜잡고 바닥을 데굴데굴 구르고, 눈물을 줄줄 흘리면서 웃었다.
192|
193|아니, 울었다.
194|
195|“으하, 으하하! 으아아아아!”
196|
197|웃음소리 대신 터져 나온 절규. 백상은 한 줌의 공력조차 실려있지 않은 주먹으로 바닥과 벽면을 후려쳤다.
198|
199|쾅! 쾅! 콰아앙!
200|
201|쉴 새 없이 쏘아지는 주먹.
202|
203|굉음과 함께 박살 난 것은 집무실뿐만이 아니었다.
204|
205|굳은살로 뒤덮인 손등이 터져 나가고, 주먹을 뒤덮은 핏물 사이로는 언뜻 새하얀 뼈가 내비쳤다.
206|
207|아프다. 그 어느 때보다.
208|
209|툭. 투두둑.
210|
211|점점이 떨어진 핏물이 거미줄처럼 갈라진 바닥에 고인다. 비틀거리며 자리에서 일어난 백상은 창가로 다가갔다.
212|
213|세상이 멈추었다고 생각한 그와는 달리, 활짝 열린 창밖 너머에서는 모든 것은 지금 이 순간에도 가파르게 돌아가고 있었다.
214|
215|“크아아악!”
216|
217|“제, 제발 죽여……!”
218|
219|- 커륵, 크르륵!
220|
221|몸과 마음을 잠식하는 마기에 저항하여 몸부림치는 인간과 짐승들.
222|
223|그리고 끔찍한 비명을 토해 내는 그들을 향해 달려나가는 크고 작은 그림자들.
224|
225|두두두두!
226|
227|지축을 울리며 무너진 석벽을 타 넘은 수많은 맹수의 무리가 그들을 덮쳤지만, 그 목적은 살육이 아닌 구조다.
228|
229|- 크아아앙!
230|
231|선두에 선 낯익은 백호의 포효와 함께 일사불란하게 움직인 맹수들이 가장 가까운 이들의 팔과 다리, 혹은 목덜미를 물고 외궁을 향해 내달렸다.
232|
233|이 끔찍한 마기에서 벗어나기 위해.
234|
235|한 걸음이라도 더, 이들을 빛으로 인도하기 위해.
236|
237|꾸국.
238|
239|한껏 말아쥔 주먹. 살갗 깊숙이 파고드는 손톱 끝에 핏방울이 비친다.
240|
241|고개를 들어 먼 곳을 응시하는 백상의 시선 끝에는 쉼 없이 뒤섞이는 빛과 어둠이 있었다.
242|
243|구구구궁!
244|
245|느껴진다. 상상할 수도 없는 거대한 힘의 파동이.
246|
247|그리고 격돌이 이어질 때마다 조금씩 사그라지는 빛과 계속해서 추락을 거듭하는 한 사람의 모습이.
248|
249|콰앙! 드드득!
250|
251|굉음과 함께 튕겨져 나온 신형이 유성처럼 지상으로 내리꽂힌다. 두 개의 전각이 무너지고 땅이 흔들린다.
252|
253|그러나 그것도 잠시. 푸른 화염은 허공을 딛고 짙은 어둠을 향해 쏘아졌다.
254|
255|단 한 순간도 쉴 새 없이. 곧 다가올 죽음조차 불태워 버릴 것처럼.
256|
257|‘진태경.’
258|
259|왜 그렇게까지 하는 것이냐, 왜.
260|
261|새어 나오지 않는 물음이 입안에 맴돈다.
262|
263|가까운 과거, 어두컴컴한 뇌옥의 한 귀퉁이에서 들었던 한 마디는 백상의 귓가에 울려 퍼지고 있었다.
264|
265|
266|
267|‘얼마나 더 많은 피를 흘릴 셈이냐, 백상.’
268|
269|
270|
271|백상은 넋 나간 눈빛으로 창밖을 바라보며 뒤늦은 대답을 건넸다.
272|
273|“모르겠구나. 나도.”
274|
275|누구에게도 말하지 못한 비밀이다.
276|
277|그는 아들을 잃은 뒤 복수를 꿈꾸었고, 남천마후를 만나 희망을 보았으며, 어느 순간 돌아올 수 없는 강을 건넌 스스로를 발견하고 절망했다.
278|
279|그리고…… 그렇게 걸어온 가시밭길의 끝에서 텅 빈 무(無)를 마주하게 되었다.
280|
281|저벅.
282|
283|백상은 비틀거리는 걸음으로 창가에서 뒷걸음질 쳤다.
284|
285|자신의 손으로 직접 그려 낸 지옥도(地獄道)를, 그 지옥도의 완성을 목숨을 바쳐 막으려는 젊은 이방인의 모습을 차마 더 이상 지켜볼 수 없었다.
286|
287|‘그 모든 것은, 무엇을 위해서였나.’
288|
289|영원히 답을 찾지 못할 의문과 함께, 창가에서 고개를 돌린 백상의 전신이 순간 석상처럼 굳었다.
290|
291|“……!”
292|
293|백상의 시선이 멈춘 곳에는 피와 먼지로 뒤덮인 한 사람이 그를 바라보고 있었다.
294|
295|모든 것을 잃고 텅 빈 껍데기가 되어 버린. 그저 높은 무위로 세월을 억누르며 괴물로 연명해 온 어느 노인의 모습을, 집무실 한구석을 차지한 커다란 면경(面鏡)이 비추고 있었다.
296|
297|하지만 백상이 본 것은 그뿐만이 아니었다.
298|

But even this lonely story had a final chapter. He opened his eyes as though waking from sleep and pushed the door wide.

[P67]
Creak.

[P68]
His spacious office came into view.

[P69]
Simple, rough furnishings that still held the warmth of their former owner. A table worn by the passing years. And a large mirror that looked out of place among them.

[P70]
And…

[P71]
That was all.

[P72]
*Nothing. There’s nothing here.*

[P73]
The realization crushed him like an immense boulder. He stared at the empty office and let out a laugh.

[P74]
“Heh. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”

[P75]
He laughed because he could not cry. Because he could do nothing else.

[P76]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress had not kept her promise. Decades of his life, everything he had done—all of it turned to ash and blew away.

[P77]
So this was how it ended.

[P78]
“Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!”

[P79]
Baeksang laughed as though he were a boy again. He clutched his stomach and rolled across the floor, tears streaming down his face.

[P80]
No. He was crying.

[P81]
“Ha—ha-ha! Aaaaaah!”

[P82]
The laughter broke into a scream. Baeksang struck the floor and walls with a fist that held not a trace of internal energy.

[P83]
Bang! Bang! Krrr-boom!

[P84]
He kept punching. The office was not the only thing that broke.

[P85]
The callused back of his hand split open. White bone showed through the blood on his fist.

[P86]
*It hurts.*

[P87]
More than it ever had.

[P88]
Drip. Drip-drip.

[P89]
Blood pooled in the spiderweb cracks across the floor. Baeksang staggered to his feet and approached the window.

[P90]
He had thought the world had stopped. Beyond the open window, everything was still moving at a furious pace.

[P91]
“Graaah!”

[P92]
“P-Please, just kill me…!”

[P93]
—Grrk, grrrk!

[P94]
People and beasts writhed as they fought the demonic qi consuming their bodies and minds. Large and small shadows raced toward them.

[P95]
Thud-thud-thud-thud!

[P96]
A host of beasts thundered over the collapsed stone wall and descended on the screaming victims—not to slaughter them, but to save them.

[P97]
—Graaaar!

[P98]
At the familiar White Tiger’s roar, the beasts moved as one. They caught the nearest people and beasts by their arms, legs, or the backs of their necks and ran toward the Outer Palace.

[P99]
Away from the demonic qi. One step farther toward the light.

[P100]
Baeksang clenched his fist. His nails dug into his palm, and blood welled around them.

[P101]
He looked into the distance, where light and darkness clashed without pause.

[P102]
Rumble!

[P103]
He could feel waves of unimaginable power. With every clash, the light faded a little more, and one figure fell again.

[P104]
Boom! Crack!

[P105]
The figure hurtled toward the ground like a meteor. Two pavilions collapsed, and the earth shook.

[P106]
A moment later, blue flame stepped on empty air and shot back toward the dense darkness.

[P107]
Without a moment’s rest. As though it could burn away even the death waiting for it.

[P108]
*Jin Taekyung.*

[P109]
*Why go so far? Why?*

[P110]
The question remained trapped in Baeksang’s mouth. Another question, heard not long ago in a corner of a dark underground prison, echoed in his ears.

[P111]
“How much more blood do you mean to spill, Baeksang?”

[P112]
Baeksang stared out the window and gave his answer at last.

[P113]
“I don’t know. I don’t know either.”

[P114]
It was a secret he had never told anyone.

[P115]
After losing his son, he had dreamed of revenge. Meeting the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had given him hope. Then one day he had realized he’d crossed a river he could never cross back, and despair had followed.

[P116]
And now, at the end of the thorny path he had walked, he found nothing at all.

[P117]
Step.

[P118]
Baeksang staggered back from the window. He could no longer bear to watch the hellscape he had made with his own hands, or the young outsider risking his life to stop it from becoming complete.

[P119]
*What was any of it for?*

[P120]
He turned away from the window with a question he would never answer—and froze.

[P121]
“…!”

[P122]
Someone covered in blood and dust was looking back at him.

[P123]
A man who had lost everything and become an empty shell. An old man who had held the years at bay through sheer martial power, surviving as a monster.

[P124]
The mirror in the corner of the office reflected him.

[P125]
But Baeksang saw something else, too.

[P126]
“Ah.”

[P127]
*Hwi.*

[P128]
He reached toward her with a call that could never reach her. Or tried to.

[P129]
The mirror’s clear, smooth surface rippled like water.

[P130]
Ssssrrrk.

[P131]
Only then did Baeksang understand who had given him the mirror, and why the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had said her promise would be fulfilled here.

[P132]
*She hadn’t lied.*

[P133]
In his cold heart, an ember of hope he had thought extinguished began to burn again.

[P134]
The mirror clouded with darkness. Before Baeksang’s trembling eyes, it spat out a black-clad figure—and a cold sword blade imbued with Force.

[P135]
Puhk!

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
Flash.

[P138]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress thrust out a foot smaller than a boy’s palm.

[P139]
The moment it met the side of my spearhead, a force greater than a giant’s surged through me.

[P140]
Crack—bang!

[P141]
—Human!

[P142]
I heard the guardian spirit’s cry as I fell. The impact drove me deep into the ground and jolted through my back, forcing my mouth open.

[P143]
Cough.

[P144]
Blood ran from the corner of my mouth. I’d already suffered serious Internal Injury, and my cracked bones creaked and ached whenever I moved.

[P145]
*Monster.*

[P146]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was a bitch for the ages, and a monster to match. Her martial arts surpassed anyone I’d faced—even the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

[P147]
But…

[P148]
*Get up. As many times as it takes.*

[P149]
A few times. A few dozen. It didn’t matter.

[P150]
There was nowhere left to retreat. One step back, and that was where hell would begin. It wouldn’t stop with me. Every living thing in Nanman, and then the Central Plains, would be swallowed by the flames.

[P151]
*I have to stop her.*

[P152]
I wiped my mouth with my sleeve and stood.

[P153]
Before I could summon my internal energy again, I realized things could still get worse.

[P154]
Rumble, rumble, rumble!

[P155]
I turned my head on instinct.

[P156]
“…Fuck.”

[P157]
Darkness was spreading over the collapsing Inner Palace.

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
